bull.b: Autoship’s high penetration and growth make demand more predictable by encouraging repeat purchases of essential pet products. This recurring mix can support customer retention, order frequency and more efficient fulfillment over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Profitability and cash generation are improving
bull.b: Margin expansion, SG&A leverage and strong free cash flow show improving operating discipline at scale. Greater cash conversion provides funding for technology, clinics and acquisitions while reducing reliance on external capital for growth initiatives.

bull.t: Pet health expansion broadens the platform
bull.b: SmartPak, Modern Animal and Vet Care extend Chewy beyond product retail into higher-value pet health services. These initiatives can broaden the addressable market, deepen customer relationships and create additional recurring purchase opportunities over time.

bear.t: Profitability remains thin for a retailer
bear.b: Despite meaningful improvement from prior losses, thin operating and net margins leave limited protection against wage, freight, fuel or promotional cost increases. A modest deterioration in demand or execution could therefore materially reduce earnings.

Slower customer acquisition can limit future order growth and reduce the pool feeding Autoship and pharmacy expansion. If weaker additions persist, Chewy may need greater marketing investment to sustain sales growth and customer engagement.

bear.t: Leverage remains meaningful for a low-margin business
bear.b: Debt provides liquidity and strategic flexibility, but leverage remains material relative to equity and a low-margin retail model. Higher interest obligations can constrain cash available for investment and increase sensitivity to operating setbacks.
